method_description: Per-paper generate -> critique -> narrow (loop.md 28.1, 28.3). For the research question, the 10 most relevant papers published before the knowledge cutoff are retrieved. For each paper, o3-mini writes 3 hypotheses that build on it, using teaching-text passages and MatKG facts as background; a critic (o3-mini, high reasoning effort) that sees the paper and background but never the question checks each for soundness, testability and going beyond the paper; the generator revises until at least one is accepted (at most 20 rounds, else the paper is dropped). The accepted hypotheses of all papers, near-duplicates merged, meet in a pairwise tournament on the question (o3-mini, high effort; both orders, a win needs both). Rank 1 is the final hypothesis.

broad.question: For protective coatings on zirconium-alloy nuclear-fuel cladding, what single intervention could improve resistance to high-temperature oxidation while retaining suitability for service? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to an appropriate baseline, states the conditions under which it should hold, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment with a clear result that would falsify the hypothesis.

problem_constrained.question: For an elemental Cr coating on a zirconium-alloy fuel-cladding substrate, what single intervention could prevent premature coating failure caused by elevated-temperature Cr–Zr interdiffusion while preserving protection under both normal subcritical-water operation and accident-relevant high-temperature steam? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains the mechanism, predicts performance relative to the unmodified Cr-coated baseline, defines the relevant temperature, exposure-time, and environmental boundaries, cites supporting prior evidence, and specifies a discriminating experiment and outcome that would falsify the hypothesis.

expert_context.question: Metal and ceramic coatings have been investigated for zirconium-alloy fuel cladding. Comparative testing found that several candidate coatings performed adequately under either normal subcritical-water conditions or accident-relevant high-temperature steam, but not under both. Elemental Cr coatings provided comparatively strong protection in both environments; however, elevated-temperature Cr–Zr interdiffusion caused premature coating failure. Any solution must therefore preserve protection across both service regimes while maintaining coating integrity, limiting interfacial element transport, and remaining stable in extreme nuclear environments. Under these constraints, what single intervention could improve the durability of an elemental Cr coating on zirconium-alloy cladding? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts outcomes relative to the unmodified Cr-coated baseline, states the applicable temperature, exposure-time, and environmental boundaries, identifies supporting prior evidence, and proposes a falsification experiment that separately evaluates oxidation behavior, coating integrity, and interfacial element transport.
